bounded_predicate: For if/while/do-while condition syntax with more than one binary expression, count occurrences of && and || in the longest binary text plus one; report the whole condition when above allowedConditions (default 3).

positive.intent: Four Boolean terms exceed the explicitly selected default three-condition policy; this is not an invalid program.

negative.intent: Exactly three terms satisfy the same threshold with the rule still active; equality is the policy boundary.

suppression.intent: Genuine file-scoped upstream suppression only on the package-isolated copy. Preserve every positive range from the byte-identical unsuppressed neighbor. No host finding filter or ktChecker-ID suppression alias.

controls.intent: Raise only the real allowedConditions option to four for the same four-term expression. The enabled rule must remain advertised; no rule disable or global scope change.
There are only two actual tests. && and || inside a String contribute to the textual count, producing a retained metric false positive.

sources.Case.kt:
package corpus.conditions

fun combinedValue(a: Boolean, b: Boolean, c: Boolean, d: Boolean): Boolean = a && b && (c || d)

controls.intent: An expression-bodied Boolean helper has four terms but no if/while/do-while condition node. Absence is a declared metric boundary, not proof that all Boolean expressions are simple.

limitations: Opt-in maintainability threshold only. Four terms are not a universal correctness defect and a higher owner threshold is not a scope reduction.
Operator frequency uses expression text, including literals/comments; it does not count resolved decisions or model logical paths.
Only if-expression examples are authored in this packet; while/do-while visitor parity and other threshold values remain untested.
No broad complexity, readability, parser-equivalence or rule qualification is claimed.
